It's just an amazing combination of flavors that makes you want to dance. For dessert, the marble cookie brownie was awkwardly cut, which actually turned out to be perfect! I ended up getting the most pieces with the cookie, which is my absolute favorite. When it's warmed up, the chocolate cookie literally melts right into the brownie in your mouth. It is so rich and gooey, and you get this perfect hint of chocolate chips that makes it taste absolutely divine. Thank you, Domino's, for being open so late!

review_text_clean: I have had repeated issues ordering from this restaurant. I order directly through their website for pickup because it's convenient, but there is no online customer support if something goes wrong. If an order is incorrect, your only option seems to be returning to the store, which isn't practical when it's raining and you only have 15 minutes left on your lunch break. On paper, this place seems like a great option with a huge selection. Unfortunately, I don't know if they're dealing with staffing issues or something else, but they frequently forget items and their quoted pickup times are often inaccurate. On my most recent order, I ordered a entree that comes with two items. I also added egg rolls and an extra soup. When I got back to my office, I discovered that half of my original meal was missing. It seems that adding extra items may have caused confusion, but that shouldn't result in part of the meal being left out. To make matters worse, the Yum Yum soup I ordered was about 25% oil. It was essentially inedible. I tried eating it anyway since half of my meal was missing, but I ended up throwing most of it away. I really want to like this restaurant because the menu is extensive and the food has the potential to be good. However, after multiple inaccurate orders and no practical way to resolve problems, I'm no longer confident ordering from them.

review_text_clean: I've been going to this pizzeria since I moved here 11 years ago, and for most of that time, I genuinely loved it. The old family who owned it provided great service, were friendly, and the pizza was always amazing. Unfortunately, since the business was sold, my experience has been completely different. From the moment we walked in, the new owner just wasn't friendly. I smiled and tried to greet him when we first came in, and he barely acknowledged us and just had a straight face. I understand that everyone has their own personality, but as a customer, you expect at least a little friendliness and basic customer service. I ordered four pizzas, and honestly, they were extremely oily and pretty mediocre, especially considering how expensive they are. I also ended up getting a huge stomach ache afterward, which made the experience even worse. The part that really bothered me, though, was what happened with the tables. This happened twice during our visit. The first time, I sat in a chair closer to the bathroom because I was waiting for it to become available. I didn't want to keep walking back and forth from our table, and the restaurant wasn't even busy. While I was sitting there, he came over and started wiping down the table even though it wasn't dirty and I was still sitting there. Then, later, my boyfriend and I were sitting at our actual table talking. We were getting ready to leave, and I was only waiting because I wanted to use the bathroom before we left, but it was still occupied. Imagine the arrogance of people to leave a negative review of an incredible historic university just because they were told NO. Then there are the handful of haters who didn't get their fannys patted whole they were students or others who got rejected.. boo hoo. Now onto the review. Fordham is an incredible university with a global reach. My wife is an alum and we are on campus all the time and are very involved with the school. First the physical campus is amazing. Rose Hill is sprawling and beautiful with a ton of green space and mature trees and plantings. The buildings are beautiful and the new student center is an amazing space. The sports facilities are great and if you have the chance you should try to get down there for a game whether it's football, basketball , water polo or even rugby. No matter what sport you go to see, it's always a great time. The staff and the students are always friendly and welcoming ! After you graduate, the connection doesn't end there. The alumni association is strong and holds events all over the country. We were in Florida and the Fordham baseball team was playing Florida Atlantic University and Fordham had an alumni tailgate at FAU before the game ! Homecoming weekend is a great time to be on campus. The tent on Edwards Parade is a great time as is the tailgate lot which is packed with Fordham pride. Homecoming always starts with the Ram Run which I proudly run each year. Academically, Fordham is stronger than ever ! Besides Rose Hill there is the Lincoln Center campus, the London Campus, the Westchester campus and even a biological field station in Westchester. Fordham also nurtures a students spiritual needs. The campus ministry is strong and well rounded. The campus church is beautiful and we attend Christmas Eve Mass there each year. Yes the tuition is expensive but you get what you pay for. The university just received a $100 million donation to build a new STEM building and increase the schools offerings I'm the sciences. The school offers a wide array of undergrad and post grad degrees and the networking of the alums allows for greater job opportunities upon graduation. Look, no school is perfect but Fordham is a fine example of Jesuit higher education and deserves a look from anyone considering higher education. Take a look at Fordham and join the Ramily!!!

First I'd like to address the negative reviews. It is a secure campus so no you can't take a walk on the closed secure campus just because you feel like it. Imagine the arrogance of people to leave a negative review of an incredible historic university just because they were told NO.

Now onto the review. Fordham is an incredible university with a global reach.
My wife is an alum and we are on campus all the time and are very involved with the school.
First the physical campus is amazing. Rose Hill is sprawling and beautiful with a ton of green space and mature trees and plantings.
The buildings are beautiful and the new student center is an amazing space.
The sports facilities are great and if you have the chance you should try to get down there for a game whether it's football, basketball , water polo or even rugby. No matter what sport you go to see, it's always a great time.
The staff and the students are always friendly and welcoming !

Homecoming weekend is a great time to be on campus. The tent on Edwards Parade is a great time as is the tailgate lot which is packed with Fordham pride.
Homecoming always starts with the Ram Run which I proudly run each year.
Academically, Fordham is stronger than ever ! Besides Rose Hill there is the Lincoln Center campus, the London Campus, the Westchester campus and even a biological field station in Westchester.
Fordham also nurtures a students spiritual needs. The campus ministry is strong and well rounded. The campus church is beautiful and we attend Christmas Eve Mass there each year.
Yes the tuition is expensive but you get what you pay for.  The university just received a  $100 million donation to build a new STEM building and increase the schools offerings I'm the sciences.
The school offers a wide array of undergrad and post grad degrees and the networking of the alums allows for greater job opportunities upon graduation.
Look, no school is perfect but Fordham is a fine example of Jesuit higher education and deserves a look from anyone considering higher education.

The Tempura Shiitakes were also excellent and definitely among our favorites. That said, some of the other dishes felt a little too focused on presentation rather than flavor. The main courses are very creative and beautifully presented, but some of them fall slightly short in terms of taste. There is also a tendency to use quite a lot of sugar, including in some of the desserts, which makes them feel overly sweet and somewhat heavy on the palate. Overall, I think there is a lot of creativity and care in the presentation, but the flavors could be a little more balanced and refined. Still, the atmosphere, service, and overall setting are absolutely wonderful, and the Butternut Squash Soup and Tempura Shiitakes alone are worth trying.

I'll gladly spend my money somewhere that values and respects its customers.

review_text_clean: Unfortunately, this experience left such a bad impression that I felt compelled to share it. My husband and I were visiting from out of town and were genuinely excited to try this restaurant for the first time. While the food itself was good, the service and overall atmosphere completely ruined our experience. Throughout our visit, we noticed servers speaking among themselves in another language while pointing in our direction, laughing, and making comments. I want to make it very clear that speaking another language was never the issue. What made us uncomfortable was the pointing, laughing, and behavior that made us feel as though we were being mocked or talked about. At one point, my husband spoke a few words to me in Spanish, and the servers began laughing again. Given everything we had already observed, it made the situation feel even more uncomfortable and disrespectful. The experience became even more upsetting when we went to pay. The restaurant only accepted cash or Venmo, so my husband paid through Venmo. When the server returned, my husband told him that the payment had been sent. The server looked at the amount and said, "Only $27?" As we were walking away, we heard him call my husband a "cheapass." That comment was completely inappropriate and disrespectful. Customers should never be insulted by staff, especially after paying for their meal. If the restaurant expected a different amount, the server could have addressed it professionally instead of making a personal insult. I cannot say with certainty what was being said during the rest of our visit, but the pointing, laughing, and final comment were enough to make us feel unwelcome and singled out. As customers, no one should have to sit through a meal wondering whether the staff is making fun of them or treating them differently because of their background. What makes this even more disappointing is that we came in with genuine excitement to enjoy the food, the culture, and the experience. Instead, we left feeling uncomfortable and disrespected. Good food means very little when the people serving it make customers feel unwelcome. Hospitality is about more than what comes out of the kitchen. It's about how you treat the people who choose to support your business. Unfortunately, what should have been a memorable dining experience for all the right reasons became memorable for all the wrong ones. We left incredibly disappointed and would not return.

review_text_clean: Overall, I would give Farra a 4.5 out of 5. Across the board, the food, hospitality and atmosphere were great. The overall venue is a little small however it is intimate, they can probably fit about 20 people inside. You have a great view of the kitchen and a good wine selection. It is a little loud when busy and can be hard to hear the person you're sitting across from but it is manageable. We ordered essential 4-5 appetizers, and 2 entrees. The apps are really what you come for. Well made, fresh, and presentable, and very prompt from order to being served. The stand out was definitely the Shrimp Ravioli, the broth was phenomenal. The Scallop Rice was amazing too, very rich in umami, very crunchy rice. The Beef Tartare was phenomenal, the sundried tomato's and sauce work so well, such a savory and rich combination. The mains were delicious and well prepared too but nothing crazy. We had the Schnitzel and the Branzino. I understand the point is to drink wine here and have a few small apps so I am not critical of mains however for the price of $52 for a breaded piece of chicken I expected a little more "wow". Maybe I'm wrong... who knows. If I went again I would just order more apps instead of a main. The service was great, we were attended to every time, drinks filled when we ran low, and never had to call our waiter over. The ONE* caveat I would add is that I just wish our waiter was dressed a little more professionally to match the aesthetic of the restaurant. He was essentially dressed as a frat kid in a tshirt and adidas sneakers. Again, this did NOT impact service once bit, but it did make a $500 dinner night feel a little cheaper. Overall a great experience and something you should 100% try.

review_text_clean: Absolute gem in Chinatown! This place is pure magic. Hidden on Elizabeth Street, this little counter-service spot serves the freshest, most gorgeous build-your-own kaisendon rice bowls I've had in NYC. You pick your toppings tuna, salmon, fluke, uni, hamachi, you name it. and they load it up over perfect rice with homemade pickles and a side of miso soup. Everything is so clean, bright, and high-quality that it honestly feels like a mini omakase in a bowl. The fish is incredibly fresh (ironic name, because nothing smells fishy here, just pure ocean goodness), the portions are generous, and the whole experience is fast, friendly, and no-fuss. Perfect for a quick but seriously elevated lunch or early dinner while exploring Chinatown. I've already told half my friends about it and I'm already planning my next visit. If you're a seafood lover, do yourself a favor and go. One of the best new spots in the neighborhood. Highly, highly recommend!

review_text_clean: One White Street is a fine restaurant that gets lots of things right. We had the alla carte menu and sampled appetizers, a pasta, and entrees, along with the bread service. The standout was the pasta...a rotelle with a very tasty filling of Swiss chard and ricotta. Also excellent was the chicken roulade; I've had heavier versions of this dish, but this one was lighter and very good. Less successful were the two salads we had...not plated in an interesting manner and pretty standard. Nothing about them was especially good nor bad. Also, the skate wasn't interesting at all...neither to look at nor to taste. The texture of the fish wasn't great and the dish felt like it needed something extra; as presented, it was dull. The tables are very close together; the room is attractive and not noisy, as there aren't many tables on each floor, and people may be keeping voices hushed so that their neighbors don't overhear. Service was friendly and very professional

Tripe was very undercooked so it was hard to chew. Spare ribs barely have any meat on them. Chicken feet and bean curd wraps were decent. Will not return. I can go to a proper Chinese restaurant to have the same dim sum meal, pay the same prices but much better quality. The restaurant and eating area are clean though, but can’t say the same about their toilet.

review_text_clean: We had high expectations for Huso after reading so many great reviews, but unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing. We spent almost $2,000 for dinner and left feeling it was nowhere near worth the price. The dinner itself was fine, but nothing particularly memorable. They were presented and recommended in a way that led us to believe they would significantly elevate the experience - since it was my birthday and our first time we decided to splurge and add it. Having enjoyed supplemental courses at Michelin-starred restaurants like Frevo, Jean-Georges, and The Modern, we expected something special. Instead, the additions did very little to enhance the meal and felt like an expensive upsell rather than a meaningful upgrade. For nearly $2,000, we expected a truly exceptional dining experience. Unfortunately, neither the food nor the supplements justified the cost. We left disappointed and regretting what we spent. Based on our experience, we would not return and would encourage others to think carefully before spending extra on the supplements.

review_text_clean: We visited Huso for a birthday celebration and unfortunately left with mixed feelings. The food presentation was beautiful, and the highlight of the meal was definitely the dessert inspired by a maple tree. It had multiple layers and different flavors, and the pecan ice cream paired with it was especially delicious and unique. We also appreciated the Polaroid photo taken for us, and one of the female servers was genuinely warm and kind enough to compliment us, which was a lovely touch. However, the service was disappointing for a birthday dinner. We were still eating our dessert when the check was brought to us, and we were asked about it twice afterward. Since the dessert had just been served and we were clearly still eating, it made us feel rushed, almost as if we were being asked to leave. Our table was also right by the entrance and hallway, which made the seating feel less comfortable and special for a birthday occasion. One of the male servers came across as noticeably unfriendly throughout the evening, and our interactions with him felt rather cold and awkward. There were also some issues with the food. The first course with caviar tasted quite fishy to both of us, and the tuna underneath looked unusually dark. I usually do not notice much fishiness in seafood, but the flavor was quite strong this time. One server also seemed to forget parts of the dish explanation while presenting it. Most of the dishes were visually impressive, but some were fairly underwhelming in flavor. We also noticed a strawberry in one of the desserts that looked wrinkled and not particularly fresh. Overall, there were definitely some memorable dishes and thoughtful touches, especially the dessert and the Polaroid photo, but the service and a few food-quality issues made the birthday experience less enjoyable than we expected. It did not feel like the special dining experience we had hoped for.

review_text_clean: Noodle Village is my go-to spot in NYC for comforting Chinese congee and classic Cantonese noodle and rice dishes! Sometimes you just want a reliable neighborhood spot that does the classics well, and this place delivers. One thing I really appreciate is that the food doesn't taste overly salty or heavy, and they don't rely on excessive seasoning or any MSG to make everything flavorful. It's comforting food that lets the ingredients shine. The congees are a must-order! My favorites are the classic century egg and pork congee, boneless shredded chicken congee, and their special Sampan congee. They're hearty, comforting, and perfect when you're craving something warm and soothing. I'm also a big fan of their beef chow fun. The noodles aren't overly oily, and they're generous with the ingredients, which makes a big difference. Their house special fried rice is another standout for me. It's not greasy, and I love the addition of unique ingredients like tiny scallops that give it extra flavor and texture. Overall, Noodle Village is a solid spot for classic Chinese comfort food without everything being drenched in oil or overloaded with salt. Whether you're craving a warm bowl of congee, wok-fried noodles, or a satisfying plate of fried rice, this is a place I keep coming back to. A dependable go-to for Cantonese comfort food in NYC!

review_text_clean: I've been a diner at this restaurant for many years, ever sinve I worked on Lafayette Street off of Prince Street. I'm vegan and having a vegan Asian restaurant nearby was helpful when I didn't have time to be home to prepare a meal. Recenlty they have not been maintaining their standards and there have been enough issues that I may need to reconsider my dining options. The floor in the restaurant was sticky and dirty to the point where it resembled a raunchy night club floor after a long night serving syrupy sweet mixed drinks to jostling, previously inebriated revelers. The tables are that kind of wood finish that ends up dirty and sticky as a result of the tops not being maintained properly and being wiped down with rags that were never sanitized and clean to begin with. I ordered a "sizzling" platter which was served decidedly not "sizzling" but rather sizzling the way an earthwom "sizzles" in the dirt after a rainstorm passes and the bright sun bears down on the parched hard-packed surface the worm has had the misfortune of finding itself on the wrong side of. The cook decided the best time to take out a bag of garbage was in the moments leading up to when I would be receiving my main course (the flacid, tepid pile of nearly uncooked saitan and undercooked tomatoes). The guy walked by my table with a heavy black plastic bag bursting with food scraps and kitchen waste, hoisting it skyward like Perseus delivering the head of Medusa to the menacing sea monster. The watress was couteous and attentive and the food was delivered in a timely manner and with an appropriate amount of skill expected from New York City waitstaff. She had the appearance of some vestal virgin vainly attempting to keep the "eternal" flame lit as the temple slowly decays and collapese around her - the last of her kind full of hopefullness that the storefront will continue to accepet eager diners willing to part with their earnings plus tips in such a way that she can come close to supporting herself in a city with a severe housin crises that is not improving. The neighborhood is gentrifying and I would say their lease will be renewed in such a way that it describes improvements to the surrounding properties. It is sad to say that this particular venue has seen its best days past and is beginning to show signs of wear and neglect and a degraded clientele. It might be best to sign off in such a way that the remaining loyal customers come away with fond memories and regret that that little vegan Asian restaurant where they used to go is no longer there.

review_text_clean: We went to Paisley for our anniversary and left already planning our return. The food was delicious, especially the Chicken Chettinad, where coconut, fennel, black pepper, and mustard seeds came together in a warm, layered heat that tingled without overwhelming. The garlic naan was about as perfect as naan gets: light, airy, warm, and full of flavor. The cocktails were just as impressive, with generous pours and intricate flavors. The Heart Beet was earthy and bright, and the Drop the Beet was smoky with a gentle kick. The Mango Misu was a standout dessert. Silky mango mousse, a bright berry compote, and soft mango jelly made for a cool, refreshing finish that balanced the spice and never felt heavy. The best part was the service, from start to finish. It felt welcoming and genuine, the kind of place where you can picture it becoming your regular spot. The owner and her husband were absolutely lovely. They made a point of wishing us a happy anniversary and stopped to chat with us, and it reminded me of a bygone era of real hospitality. It has the warmth of a mom-and-pop place inside a modern Manhattan restaurant, where you wouldn't expect to find it. Definitely a gem. We'll be back for sure.

review_text_clean: Easy to find on Bowey st. In Manhattan's Chinatown (1/2 block south of the iconic Canal st). Looks a little plain on the outside. They sport roasted ducks in the windows (which is a famous look, in many NYC Chinatown restaurants). The restaurant has a "box car" layout. There are about 5 family style tables ( holding 8 - 10 people) and an additional 3-4 smaller, 1 or 2 person tables. The paper menu is huge and looks like a typical Chinese takeout menu. The options are tremendous and have many styles to choose from. Each table starts with a customery endless pot of tea. The speed and serving sizes was surprising. We were a table of 6 and in about 10 minutes, the orders started coming out to us. Everyone was served within 15 minutes. My friends ordered chicken and pork, beef and seafood dishes. My friend Jenny (a Manhattan Chinatown born and raised native) ordered seafood on crispy noodles. She shared some with 3 of us and still had alot for herself. I tasted one of the shrimps. It was a big tasty shrimp, marinated in congee sauce. I was surprised there was so much, in an individual serving plate. Another person ordered a wonton noodle dish, which looked like a 2 - 3 pound bowl. I bet she couldn't finish it (although she did). MY MEAL; I ordered the roasted duck (seoi siu aap - in Cantonese) on white rice. Like the others, my meal came out in about 10 minutes and was a huge dish. There were 10 large pieces of duck layed, on a fluffy bed of white rice, with a sided of steamed vegetables. The duck was a bit plain. Although, when I added "THEIR" soy sauce on it, the flavour was better. I said "THEIR" soy sauce because, it was sweeter than most soy sauces and it was a "tad" bit thicker. This is a soy sauce you'll want to take home. Actually, the fact that the duck came without sauce is a good thing. I've had duck in the past and the sauce did not always agree to my liking. The meat was tender and succulent. On the whole, it was better than"marginally good" Be clear, I definitely enjoyed it down to the last bite. It just didn't stand out from the other roasted duck dishes out there. A strange (still ok) thing; there weren't any fortune cookies? 🤔They did however, have "Chinese doughnuts" - for $2.50. It's an oversized wobbly shaped doughnut, 3X the size of a normal doughnut with confectionery sugar. This was a first for me, it being more a novelty. The big shock, was the bill. With separate checks, I had roasted duck on white rice and a Chinese beer. With tax, the bill came out to $14.50! With what I got, I thought this was going to be a $20 bill,( just for the food alone). My friend Jenny said, at the end of the meal, this restaurant is her favorite. She explained, she always has enough leftovers, to take home and the price is great. This restaurant is a few blocks away from the court houses in lower Manhattan and can get predictably crowded, during the lunch hour. We went on a Sunday, with mostly families at the other tables. We got a table immediately. The kitchen was small and well kept. It was nice to see my meals were coming from a properly kept kitchen. Whilst dining, the kitchen brought out bulk items of food, were they assemble the meals, up front, by the window, for take out orders. This is a fun way to see what else is on the menu. The waiters are all Chinese, speaking Cantonese and Mandarin. If they stumble on English, there's always someone there to help. Please please don't be insulted by their manners, as sometimes they come off abrupt and short (even if you are Chinese). It's a Chinese/Chinatown restaurant "thing". Throughout time, I've become used to it and I don't even notice there manners anymore. Come tip time, I still give a generous tip anyway (they're still hard working people, with small wages). Dine in or takeout, check out NB Wing Wong, you'll be happy. P.S. Their online prices are higher than their in person prices.

review_text_clean: Cool and Lovely Concept, but Unfriendly Staff I've been a regular at The Lost Draft in Chinatown, and I've genuinely loved this place. I've always been respectful of their two-hour policy, consistently ordering drinks at least every two hours, often with a pastry, and tipping 20% or more. I've even contributed positive messages to their wall because I genuinely appreciate the concept and atmosphere they've created for film and theater artists. Unfortunately, today's experience left me feeling quite disappointed. I needed to step outside briefly to take a phone call. Despite there being plenty of empty tables inside, a staff member came outside specifically to tell me that I needed to move my belongings from the four-person table I was occupying to a smaller one. I explained that I would be back in just a few minutes, but he insisted that I move my things immediately. I understand that businesses have seating policies, and I have no problem respecting reasonable rules. What bothered me was the manner in which this was communicated. The staff member came across as unnecessarily rigid, unfriendly, and lacking in basic understanding, especially given that the café was far from full. What makes this particularly disappointing is how much I've appreciated and supported this place. I've consistently respected their policies and contributed to the welcoming atmosphere they're trying to cultivate. I don't expect special treatment for being a regular, but I do think every customer deserves to be treated with basic courtesy and a little flexibility. It's a shame when a place with such a thoughtful, lovely concept falls short in the way it treats its customers. A welcoming atmosphere isn't just about the décor, the drinks, or the messages on the wall. It's also about how people are made to feel. I still appreciate what The Lost Draft is trying to create, but today's interaction made me feel considerably less welcome in a place I've genuinely enjoyed spending time in.

review_text_clean: This is exactly what you want from a sit down Chinese restaurant. Delicious, American Chinese food (unless you can read the Chinese menu and unlock the interesting stuff) done very, very well. We had the beef chow fun and the lychee pineapple duck. The chow fun was dang near perfect. The only note I have is that it was a drop salty. Otherwise, perfect. The wok hei (that hard to quantify smoky flavor when you get really good Chinese food) is always what brings this dish together, and it was really kicking in this disk. The beef was tender but not falling apart, a good bite but not chewy. The bean sprouts were crisp and satisfying. The duck was really a work of art. It's a very fatty dish, but the fat under the skin was perfectly rendered, and it melted in my mouth. The sauce was sweet without being sickly, and mixed very well with the white rice that came in the side. The skin on the duck was excellent. It's tossed in a sauce so it's not crispy, but it was so savory and flavorful. Hop Kee is legendary for a reason. Not because the food is revolutionary, but because there's a comfort and beauty in a single thing done well.

review_text_clean: Double Crispy is one of my fave Chinatown bakeries; I've been coming here since 2018. Whenever I am in Chinatown, I try to stop by and pick up a couple things. Their variety of baos, baked goods, cakes, and egg tarts is incredible! Every year they put so much love and care into their moon cakes for mid autumn moon festival, and around lunar new year, they have endless traditional, lunar new year treats, and sweets for you to purchase. The staff is friendly and efficient. My personal faves are their moon cakes, Portuguese style egg tarts, sesame cookies (the thin flat ones at the front), the cha siu bao, pork floss bao, and the pineapple bao with egg custard inside! Their HK style sponge cake is also a hit; my 4-yo is obsessed with it! You can also get their packs or chicken/cabbage bao for an amazing value, which I occasionally get. They keep well in the freezer, and when you want, you can pop some Out, steam them, and they are super fresh and fluffy! Love this family owned business. Their story (as featured by NYT food on YouTube) is just so touching and heart warming. How can you not want to support them?!

Double Crispy is one of my fave Chinatown bakeries; I’ve been coming here since 2018. Whenever I am in Chinatown, I try to stop by and pick up a couple things. Their variety of baos, baked goods, cakes, and egg tarts is incredible! Every year they put so much love and care into their moon cakes for mid autumn moon festival, and around lunar new year, they have endless traditional, lunar new year treats, and sweets for you to purchase. The staff is friendly and efficient. My personal faves are their moon cakes, Portuguese style egg tarts, sesame cookies (the thin flat ones at the front), the cha siu bao, pork floss bao, and the pineapple bao with egg custard inside! Their HK style sponge cake is
also a hit; my 4-yo is obsessed with it! You can also get their packs or chicken/cabbage bao for an amazing value, which I occasionally get. They keep well in the freezer, and when you want, you can pop some
Out, steam them, and they are super fresh and fluffy! Love this family owned business. Their story (as featured by NYT food on YouTube) is just so touching and heart warming. How can you not want to support them?!

review_text_clean: Was looking for a good coffee shop in the area and came across La Colombe Coffee Roasters. I had tried La Colombe before, so I brought my friends here to check it out as well. Service was super quick, and everyone was really nice, from the server to our barista. I decided to try one of their seasonal drinks, the Iced Pumpkin Spice Draft Latte with oat milk. Their Draft Latte is a creamy, smooth cold coffee drink, and the pumpkin spice gives it that warm seasonal flavour without completely overpowering the coffee. The oat milk also made it extra smooth and creamy. Definitely a nice fall drink. My friends tried a few different drinks as well: Matcha Vanilla - The matcha was actually really good, with a nice balance between the earthy matcha and sweetness from the vanilla. Neither flavour overpowered the other. Caramel Apple Latte - A nice combination of coffee, caramel and apple flavours. It had a good balance of sweetness and coffee, with the apple adding a subtle fruity touch rather than making it taste overly sweet. Iced Vanilla Latte - Pretty much true to its name! A straightforward iced latte with a clear vanilla flavour. Simple, refreshing, and exactly what you'd expect. The café itself was clean and has a smaller, cozy setup with around 7 stools for seating, along with a bench running along the entire back wall. It seems like a good spot to grab a quick coffee or sit for a little while. Overall, a quick and pleasant visit with friendly service and a good selection of drinks. The seasonal Pumpkin Spice Draft Latte was definitely a fun one to try.

review_text_clean: I've been a longtime patron of Weather Up both at the Vanderbilt Ave location and at Tribeca. Somehow they manage to come up with a drink that mirrors the weather outside or the mood I am in. The Two Time I had yesterday for example was perfect for the strange transitional weather we're having straddling both the stubborn humidity and the chilly undercurrent. I also remember a time in 2018 when I was having an extraordinary bad day at the office I showed up and mentioned my plight to the bartender at Vanderbilt and he whipped me (I think) a Barrymore Room that was the perfect pick me up. The Charleston from a year or two ago was my go to drink. For my birthday in 2022, I ordered a Ramos Gin Fizz expecting to be turned down (because it's an absurd order) and it was made for me. Special plaudits for remaining walk in only, and not pressuring me and my guests to leave at a certain time. This creates a space where we enjoy drinking at a comfortable pace in a comfortable setting. The service has always been stellar from everyone I have ever interacted with: attentive, friendly, and never pushy. I feel that dining and drinking in New York City has become increasingly oppressive with Resy reservations, time limits, and an experience that makes a night out feel like I'm at a theme park. Thank you for being an oasis of civilization in an algorithm based dining hellscape. Weather Up has been and will continue to be at the top of my list when I want a cocktail with friends or date nights. It's everything I would want in a bar.

review_text_clean: Little Italy is one of those New York neighborhoods where, every once in a while, you find a place that feels like a passage to the past, and Caffe Roma is exactly that. Founded in 1891, this cafe has managed to preserve something that is increasingly difficult to find in New York: the feeling of another era. In the middle of all the noise, movement, and constant change of the city, stepping inside feels like entering a little time capsule. And yes, the coffee is excellent, but Caffe Roma is about more than just coffee. Take a moment to look around. The details on the walls, the ceiling, the old-fashioned décor... they are all part of the experience. This place has been collecting stories for more than a century, and you can feel that history while sitting at your table, enjoying a coffee and an Italian dessert. With just a little imagination, you might even travel back in time for a few minutes. My personal favorite is the affogato. I love the combination of hot espresso and cold, creamy vanilla gelato, and this is exactly the kind of place where it just feels right to order one. But you really can ́t go wrong here. Whether you are looking for a good coffee, something sweet, or a traditional Italian dessert, there are plenty of options to enjoy. Whether you are visiting New York for the first time or you are a local who has walked throught Little Italy a hundred times, Caffe Roma is one of those places worth experiencing at least once. Not only for what you ́ll taste, but for the little trip throught time that comes with it.

review_text_clean: In NYC standard (both price and quality wise), nice semi-high-end sushi place worth giving it a shot. It's not a typical omakase place where you sit down at the counter and the chef serves you a piece by piece. The way how they serve the dishes is much more that of typical restaurant but ambience of the pysical space is like good fine-dining spot. They do have sushi menu called Chef's selection (which is basically what omakase means in Japanese) and it is basically 6 pieces of sushi served in one plate, all in just one serving. What this means is that, compared to typical type of omakase being served a piece by piece, freshness of the sushi is relatively not as good. How big one thinks that "relative difference" is probably differs for everyone. In my personal opinion, it was a marginal sacrifice that I would be willing to take for enjoying good fining-dining NYC restaurant ambience cause still delicious sushi. So I am certainly willing to revisit. This isn't your typical omakase restaurant where you sit at the counter and your sushi is served one by one. The overall atmosphere, service, and presentation feel more like a typical fine dining restaurant. Because the sushi is served all at once, the freshness of the sushi can feel a bit, or somewhat, lower than omakase sushi, where you can watch your pace as you eat. Personally, I liked the restaurant's atmosphere, and the sushi was delicious enough that I'd definitely come back. However, I'm a bit skeptical about Korean tourists. I generally think Korean tourists find Japanese food in New York City to be a very poor value for money experience. Korea's proximity to Japan means a generally high level of understanding and quality of Japanese cuisine, and the extensive use of seafood. Therefore, I believe that decent Japanese food in New York can be found at a much lower price in Korea. This is especially true with the high exchange rate.

review_text_clean: I loved this place so much I ate here multiple times during my trip to NY! Their wide hand pulled noodles are fantastic. I've had the Northwest Mutton Noodles in Soup, Braised Beef Noodle in Soup, Northwest Lamb Noodle and the Spicy Pork Intestines Noodles in soup. All of them were delicious. You choose your spice level when ordering, from none to extra spicy. There's chili oil, soy sauce, vinegar and raw garlic at the counter. I recommend adding some vinegar, takes it up another notch making it even better. Their portions are much larger than other restaurants in the Chinatown area and every bowl I got ranged from $12-$13. It's a stall located inside Mott Street Eatery so no tipping required. They give a discount for paying in cash. Fantastic food and a fantastic value!

I definitely won't be coming back to this location again.

As you can see from the menu in the photo, the Yakult series DOES come in a large size, so there was nothing unusual or confusing about me ordering a large 葡萄多多. I never said 葡萄啵啵 or 葡萄冰沙.

And honestly, the grape slush tasted terrible too. It basically tasted like flavorless blended ice with some grape syrup poured into it. That was it. I definitely would never have ordered this drink on purpose.

The staff very reluctantly agreed to remake my drink, but instead of fixing the order they got wrong, she continued making drinks for people who ordered after me first. I definitely won’t be coming back to this location again.

review_text_clean: I've been to all 3-star restaurants in New York, not to mention in Portugal, France, SF. I've also been to Jungsik 3~4 times, before they received a Michelin star. I'll say that this most recent visit was the most disappointing and I'm baffled at how they're maintaining 3 stars. Our entire meal, we were rushed through each course. Our waiter kept hovering and kept prodding me to eat more quickly. I've never been treated like this at any Michelin star restaurant. He would also frequently interject to make sure we weren't touching or disturbing the decorations on the plating or eating things in the wrong order. I understand that the chef would appreciate guests eating the dishes with intention and mindfulness, but this was over the top. The forced pace was extremely unpleasant and ruined our evening. Also, I've never in my life been asked to leave or vacate a table at any 3-star Michelin restaurant? Other places seem to know and accept that if we're spending literally thousands of dollars on a meal, that we should be able to sit and enjoy our meal, and even perhaps linger after eating 10 courses. We weren't ready to end the evening, since it was for my friend's 30th birthday, so we literally just stood outside the restaurant after we were ushered out, for about another 20 minutes, standing in slightly chilly weather to finish catching up. We weren't even offered coffee or tea with dessert to sit and enjoy. Even as we were leaving, the dozens of waitstaff kept brusquely asking us to clear the walkway and stand off to the side. We also had asked the kitchen to hold onto some personal items, that we asked them to retrieve for us at the end of the night, and they also completely forgot or misplaced the items, so we were standing (yet again) by the hostess for another 10-15 minutes simply waiting for someone to notice. Honestly, the food was also quite salty across multiple courses, but overall good. Less impressive than previous visits - menu could use a revamp. I think I had the same uni rice dish 7~8 years ago. Overall, service was pretty appalling.

review_text_clean: Jungsik is undoubtedly an impressive culinary experience, and the cuisine is the strongest part of the evening. The dishes were beautifully executed and presented with exceptional attention to detail. Flavors were deep, complex and very carefully balanced. For me, the standout was the opening sequence of banchan - genuinely memorable and one of the highlights of the entire dinner. There was a great sense of creativity and precision in the food. Having dined at a number of three-Michelin-starred restaurants, however, I found the service at Jungsik somewhat below the level I have come to expect at this category of restaurant. Everyone was perfectly polite and professional, but at this level, hospitality is about more than being courteous and explaining the ingredients. At restaurants such as Noma, Geranium, Disfrutar or L'Arpège, I have experienced a much more natural interaction with the guests - a feeling that the team is genuinely engaging with you and reading the table, rather than simply delivering the service. A small detail, but one that I found particularly unfortunate, was receiving the bill while I was still drinking my coffee. In a restaurant of this caliber, I would expect the end of the meal to feel completely unhurried. Instead, it gave me the impression that the table was ready to be turned over and that I should leave. I also noticed that as the dining room became busier, the movement of the service team became noticeably faster and somewhat nervous. This created a sense of urgency that, in my opinion, does not quite fit the atmosphere I expect from a three-star dining room, where service should ideally feel calm, effortless and almost invisible. The desserts were, for me, the least convincing part of the menu. As with everything else, the presentation was impeccable, but the flavors did not leave the same impression as the savory courses. Overall, Jungsik delivers an excellent and highly refined culinary experience. The food absolutely demonstrates the level of ambition and technical precision expected from a restaurant of this stature. For me, however, the hospitality did not quite reach the same level as the cuisine. And once the food is operating at such a high level, it is precisely these seemingly small details of service that make the difference between an excellent dinner and a truly exceptional three-star experience.

review_text_clean: Overhyped, underwhelming, and absolutely not the "best happy hour in NYC" experience we were promised. We stopped by Arlo Rooftop at Arlo SoHo for anniversary cocktails and appetizers before dinner, and the service was so poor we left after one round. Great concept, disappointing execution. The ambiance: The rooftop itself has potential, with a mix of lounge seating, high-tops, open space, greenery, and string lights. The interior felt a bit empty, but the rooftop could be a nice setting for drinks. The experience: * Seating: We arrived around 4:15 PM on a Friday to a very light crowd and were seated at a table that was legitimately in a bush. We politely asked to move to the adjacent table, only to be told it was reserved for a party arriving in 2.5 hours. I explained we planned to stay only an hour or two, but there was zero flexibility or effort to accommodate us. Not a great first impression. * Drinks: My husband ordered a happy hour beer, and I ordered the Vinho Verde from the main menu, which was their most expensive drink option. Given the light crowd, our anniversary reservation, and the fact that we weren't exclusively ordering from the happy hour menu, I expected a little more attentiveness. * Service: We waited 20 minutes without receiving either drink. I eventually walked inside to check on them, at which point our waitress noticed me and gestured toward the bartender. The drinks finally arrived a few minutes later. The Vinho Verde tasted off to me, almost as though the bottle had been open too long, though I can't say for certain. * Follow-up: The most frustrating part? We weren't checked on again. Not once. We would have happily ordered another round and some appetizers, but after about an hour with our waitress having acknowledged us only once, we decided to leave. Bottom line: we got an awkward table, a 20-minute wait for drinks, and virtually nonexistent service. The setting has potential, but hospitality matters just as much as the view. The rooftop was recommended to us as a top NYC happy hour spot from Google & chatGPT, but our experience was nowhere close. There are too many great places in this city to spend your time chasing down drinks. I won't be back.

Giving zero stars if I could:
I was at holywater and received the WORST customer service from the manager on duty. I had asked him about two items on my bill that I know* I was wrongly charged. Mind you, we had a relatively large group of people ordering different drinks and food. We wanted to keep separate tabs going for everyone. I paid my tab but then the server told me that “he doesn’t really know what’s going on” but $60 is left. Reluctantly, I had to pay it (and tipped again). I texted myself the receipt to take a close look and something wasn’t right. I asked our group who ordered lalo tequila and kettle one martini? The answer: no one. So I brought it to the manager’s attention as a mistake. Wow. He could not have been more defensive. I asked him what Lalo was and he said that’s the tequila I ordered. When I said I was the only one who had margaritas in the group and never asked for Lalo, he said that’s not true I brought it to you. I was shocked. If it wasn’t for our friend’s birthday and trying not to ruin the evening, believe me, I would have gone the distance because it’s absolutely absurd. We were coming to him with a clear mistake and he refused to acknowledge the servers’ error on their part and then THREW a member of our party under the bus as the culprit why the tab became so confusing. He tried to smooth over the situation by wishing us a “goodnight” and an itemized receipt - but what do we need that for if you’re not going to acknowledge the 2 drinks we told you we didn’t order? Unbelievable and so inappropriate. We already paid for our food and drinks and we’re telling him that there is a mistake - he didn’t oblige. Won’t be coming back ever and will spread the worst about the awful service.

review_text_clean: Lei on Doyers Street is easily one of the most exciting dining spots in Chinatown. The space is warm, intimate, and atmospheric, with bottle-lined walls and a relaxed neighborhood energy that sets the tone right away. The kitchen balances precision with depth across every plate: the chilled celtuce starter delivers a crisp, bright snap in an aromatic red dressing, the raw fish is delicate and cleanly dressed, and the crispy soft-shell crab hits the mark with great crunch beneath a rich, savory sauce. Beyond the food, the low-intervention wine list is the real star-drinking a bottle of Domaine de L'Anglore Pierre Chaude alongside these flavors shows just how natural wines and modern Chinese cooking belong together. Service is knowledgeable, attentive, and down-to-earth. An absolute gem for a quiet date or sharing a stellar bottle with good company.

review_text_clean: Café Fig - A Wonderful New Addition to SoHo! What a wonderful little café that recently opened on the corner of Broome and Mott! Café Fig brings something special to the neighborhood with its Greek-inspired coffee and creative beverages. The owner, George, is an awesome, laid-back guy who makes you feel right at home. I ordered the Freddo Cappuccino and the Banana Churro, and both were fantastic. The Freddo Cappuccino was done exactly how I'd imagine a proper Greek-style coffee should be, with that beautiful, creamy foam and a little touch of honey. Excellent! The Banana Churro was such a treat! Light, flavorful, and surprisingly refreshing, with a unique banana milk flavor. Almost like having dessert in a cup without being overly heavy or sweet. Definitely one of the more interesting drinks I've had recently. Beyond the drinks, I really appreciate the attention to detail throughout the café. It's cute, quaint, and thoughtfully designed. The rich maroon interior, inspired by the color of a fig, gives the space a warm and distinctive personality. You can tell a lot of intention went into creating it. And as a bonus, it's right next to a great bánh mì spot! Grab your morning or afternoon coffee at Café Fig, then finish the day with a delicious bánh mì next door. Not a bad combination! Definitely recommend stopping by and saying hi to George. It's exciting to have another independent café in the neighborhood, especially one that's doing Greek coffee right. Welcome to SoHo, Café Fig!

review_text_clean: ((4.5 stars)) an art cafe hidden in plain sight of Atelier Jolie, an arts collective / cultural center in NoHo, which was opened by Angelina Jolie. those in the arts scene might recognize the address as it was occupied by Andy Warhol and Jean-Michael Basquiat a long time ago...and it's formerly the home of the speak-easy-ish restaurant Bohemian. Eat Offbeat operates the cafe area and is an NYC-based organization that employs refugees and immigrants to celebrate and elevate the craft & artisanship of cooking from around the world. the cafe space feels like an art gallery--adorned with art and art-centric books, somewhat intimate seating, and bright art lighting positioned above. the ambiance evokes upscale with the touch of minimalism in the bare white walls but is welcoming in its curated cafe menu of coffees, teas, juices, and small bites. it's clear that the decor and vibe are to evoke creativity and thought as you enjoy a coffee or a bite. very much place to share, but also to protect its ethos of spirit. been here several times - enjoyed a cortado and Americano to-go. both were made proficiently. currently, the cafe uses a South American (maybe El Salvadoran?) medium roast coffee that has a pleasant deep nuttiness and a mildly sweet undertones as a coffee. very much a smooth caffeine for the winter times. the last time i stopped here, ordered a Turkish coffee and enjoyed it at the cafe. not sure the "Turkish coffee" is actually traditional coffee from Turkey, but the coffee served in a Turkish style. it's served on a small silver tray where a "cezve" (the handled counter where the coffee is boiled), fincan (the small 2 oz. cup) for slowly sipping the coffee, and a Syrian Barazak Cookie (there are two choices of sweets). it's very much an aesthetically pleasing presentation. the coffee is served hot as it foams up...the coffee tastes richer and thicker because it is served this way. it's fancy in a nonchalant way. review_text_clean: I used to study and work near Cocoron so it has a very nostalgic place in my heart. That being said, it's been a decade since I last dined here and a lot seems to have changed within that time (although the fact that they are walk in and cash only has not changed). Their previous location closer to Chinatown/SoHo had a railroad-style layout making it narrow and cramped with people waiting in line. This location is spacious in comparison with plenty of table seating and we did not have to wait to be seated during lunch time on a weekday. Their menu has expanded a lot to include appetizers and seasonal specials outside of their Japanese soba roots - not sure I'm a fan of that to be honest but I think it's their attempt to accommodate a wider demographic. I ordered the vegan version of their signature mera mera noodles, extra spicy. The broth was rich and noodles plenty, but the amount of toppings was sparse - a few sprigs of bok choy, beansprouts, and crumbled tofu....super disappointing. Next time, I would try something else. And for those with a high spice tolerance - no, their extra spicy was not spicy. I'm still attached to this place because of the memories I have with it, but the quality of food has gone down compared to how they were 10 years ago.

review_text_clean: After navigating a narrow alleyway illuminated by mysterious and slightly thrilling neon lights, and passing an ID check (a passport is recommended), you open a hidden door to discover a luxurious and classical space completely unexpected from the outside. Surrounded by heavy velvet sofas, opulent chandeliers, and classic paintings, you feel as if you've stumbled into a secret party during the Prohibition era of the 1920s. The unique style of serving drinks in teacups and mugs (a remnant of the Prohibition era when establishments disguised themselves as cafes to avoid detection) is also distinctive and playful. The atmosphere is superb, making it perfect for a special night while traveling. The "hidden gem" feel, located in a slightly hard-to-find spot, made for a fantastic experience. It wasn't crowded because it was a weekday night.

review_text_clean: If ambiance matters most when you visit a restaurant, you won't be disappointed. While the tables are squeezed a bit too close for my taste, I'm a sucker for contemporary artwork and exposed brick. And this, dear reader, concludes the complimentary portion of my review. We were willing to overlook the extended wait for a server to come to our table and take our order. But service is where everything connected to our evening steadily rolled downhill. First, it seems only one person was serving the entire restaurant. And while I won't get into details about the actual service, suffice it to say it was about as good as the akra appetizer we ordered. So, we placed our order: two apps and two entrees. We both stuck to water. My cousin ordered a cranberry juice (more on this later) but they had none that evening. Not only did the apps take forever to reach our table, there was maybe a 20 minute gap between the 1st and 2nd app. The akra, while beautiful, was bland. And the pikliz (more on this later) didn't elevate the taste. We also ordered wings with a spicy mango sauce. The sauce tasted more like a splashed on afterthought than an integrated element. Again, it wasn't terrible, but it wasn't memorable. Let's move on to the entrees: goat and griot. Thought was definitely put into the presentation and both proteins were tender as a muh. So tender they made our mouths water. So, you can't imagine our disappointment when we dug into our plates. Everything tasted like a shadow of the flavors that raised us. The side of pikliz (seriously, wait till I tell tale) didn't help, accentuate or elevate the dish--it was just added heat. And, quick side note: we added one side after we got our entrees, which...never made it to the table. Oh, and someone was celebrating a birthday that night. A fact the DJ refused to let us forget. Have I been living under a rock? I had no idea there were so many genres and versions of Happy Birthday. And he must have played all of them at a volume OSHA would fine for such a small space. We finish our food and get our check--and not because we ordered the check. We weren't asked if we wanted dessert, which I did. Being as greedy as I am, I had my eye on the pain patat. But without prompting from our table we get a check. The cranberry juice they didn't have? It was on the check. The side we ordered that never made it to our table? It was on the check. To add insult to injury, they charged separately for the pikliz. THE PIKLIZ?! But what really and truly blackened my djon djon was the automatic gratuity. Now, I just reviewed the menu to make sure. Nowhere inside or outside the restaurant (that I can remember) or on the menu was an advisory about automatic gratuity. I've eaten at restaurants that add automatic gratuity, but usually not for a table of 2 and always with obvious signage. My review not withstanding. I really wanted to like this place. I wanted this to be the cool new Haitian restaurant I put my people on to. But there was just too much for me to ignore. I understand that my review is an anomaly. You would be hard pressed to find a one- or two-star review for the restaurant. So either I caught them on a bad night or I'm making mountains out of mole hills.

The hostess was bright, friendly and seated us promptly! Unfortunately, the rest of the service was very below expectations. Our server barely came to the table. We were promptly given water as soon as we sat down from the bussers/water servers, but didn't get greeted or our orders taken from our server for at least 10 minutes which is unacceptable. He also didn't introduce himself or ask if we've visited before which is expected at a restaurant with this price point. Once we got our drinks (not brought out by our server) we waited another 20 minutes to even order. He never came by. I also was hesitant to ask for his recommendation because he couldn't really explain my question earlier about what spritz was most popular - he was talking about the "fuzzy" juice but I had no idea what that meant. Our food arrived in a timely manner and was delicious. Again, brought out by the bussers. Nobody came to quality check. We finished and our plates were cleared by the busser. Our drinks were never offered to be refilled, weren't cleared and sat empty on our table for 20 minutes. I had to flag down a busser to order another round. I really hope you can learn from this and improve and hopefully improve the service standards at Dante and that this was hopefully a one-off occurrence.

I also was hesitant to ask for his recommendation because he couldn't really explain my question earlier about what spritz was most popular - he was talking about the "fuzzy" juice but I had no idea what that meant.

Our food arrived in a timely manner and was delicious. Again, brought out by the bussers. Nobody came to quality check. We finished and our plates were cleared by the busser. Our drinks were never offered to be refilled, weren't cleared and sat empty on our table for 20 minutes. I had to flag down a busser to order another round. I tried to order a pinot grigio which I was then surprised that Dante didn't carry it according to the server. I asked for a glass of sauv blanc and a cup of ice on the side explicitly. Our drinks came out (via a busser), no ice in sight. I asked the busser for ice and he promptly brought it out. Then, we were seated outside and the 2-top beside us cleared and was reseated a 3-top (which was absolutely not appropriate for the table size) and the woman on the edge of the table's chair and hair was literally rubbing up on our table and my sister couldn't get up to go to the restroom.

I had to stand up and go up to a busser to ask for the check. The server never came back.

The bussers did a great job but our server not so much.

I really hope you can learn from this and improve and hopefully improve the service standards at Dante and that this was hopefully a one-off occurrence.

review_text_clean: Proper ramen on the Lower East Side. Just don't come on a hot day. It's a small, cosy shop with an open kitchen and no air con. On a hot afternoon it was like a sauna, and I left soaked through. The menu is short, which is always a good sign for a little ramen shop. I had the clam and mushroom, and my partner had the new Tokyo style. Both were quality bowls. The broth is rich and well made, and the chicken was tender and juicy. The noodles were OK, but a little strong on the alkaline taste. The egg was short on flavour, and portions are on the small side. Service was quick and the cold water kept coming, which was a lifesaver in that heat. It's comfortably better than the chain ramen places and above average overall. It's still not my favourite bowl abroad though. That goes to RamenMe in Porto. Solid, well-made ramen at a fair price. Recommended, but it's best on a cooler day.

review_text_clean: Cotti Coffee is a small corner coffee shop parked ion Clinton Street. modern decor with warm wood tones and a clean to the eyes feel. definitely leans into the modern customer as ordering via app or touchscreen kiosk is emphasized...but you can order in-person as well. the shop is new and clean. there are a few small. tables to sit at...but most people seem to grab and go. you can't add your own sweetener or dairy (or non-dairy) creamer to the drinks as that has to be done by the barista--i assume this is to reduce waste and save money. the drinks menu is pretty large with a variety of coffee and tea drinks that can be served hot or iced. stopped here twice, recently, and grabbed an iced Americano (dark roast gold) which was fine and did the job of my getting my caffeine fix, but i prefer the medium roast which is more my speed in terms of taste and made for a smooth icy coffee drink on a warm afternoon. the service is friendly and quick. of course, i went here when it was a slower time of the day...not sure how speedy service is when drink orders pile up. all that said, the app is easy to use and you can do some customization on your drinks, but this place is built on quick serve coffee drinks not overly complex orders. very much modern quick serve versus an artisan coffee shop experience as the drinks seem to be made via a touchscreen coffee machine and then are finished by the staff. overall, it's nice option when you want solid coffee at a fair price and have the option to order by phone ahead of time for pickup or delivery.

review_text_clean: We had a wonderful experience at KALYE, a Filipino restaurant in New York that I highly recommend. We enjoyed traditional dishes served on banana leaves, which added a special touch to our meal. At KALYE, you have the option to eat with your hands or use clear plastic gloves-both ways are enjoyable! The owner, Mr. Rob Mallari-D'Auria, was very engaging and made a point to visit each table to inquire about our experience and introduce himself. When he came to our table, we had the joy of sharing our Filipino heritage with him. My brother mentioned that we were born in the Philippines, which led to lots of laughter as we switched from English to Tagalog-except for my son, who was born here and hasn't learned Tagalog or our dialect, Pangalatok. Mr. Rob was generous and offered us a complimentary shot, which was delightful, along with an amazing Ube Mocktail! I can't recommend the Ube sliders enough; they are a must-try for anyone planning to visit. Overall, the food was fantastic, and the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. The staff, including Mr. Rob, were incredibly friendly and attentive. I will definitely be returning to KALYE for another wonderful meal! ---

Despite arriving at 3:10 PM (past the 3:00 PM check-in time), I was unable to use the iPad check-in because I hadn't received a room number yet. When I asked for an ETA, I was simply told to come back in 20 minutes. I returned around 3:30pm and spoke with another staff member who gave a vague answer. Given the inconvenient delay that nearly made me late for an uptown reservation at 5pm, I asked if a late check-out could be accommodated for my departure day. I was told they couldn't approve it at the desk and I'd have to call down later. No gesture or accommodation was offered to alleviate the inconvenience, making for a poor first impression. To top it off, when I finally got to the room, the robes and slippers I requested three weeks prior were missing. Ultimately, I've had much better service and hospitality at other New York City hotels, and unfortunately, I will not be returning.

review_text_clean: This is a really shiny hotel that you might be better off staying away from. Travel + Leisure said this was a cool hotel. Okay. I tried to book online. I got a confirmation screen, but no email or card charge notification, so I tried again after 10 mins (do not do this, it was dumb of me). Got a second confirmation screen, but again, no email or card charge. Tried to call twice, but couldn't get through to a real person, so I guess I'll have to go there. I'm there. Yep, there are two reservations under my name! Luckily the person at the front desk was very kind and canceled one for me. To their credit, everyone at Public was very nice and tried to be helpful. I check into my room; it was very cold and I'd booked this hotel specifically to get a bath. I try the bath; the knob is weird and the spigot won't work. Call the front desk; they're sending an engineer. Harris, the engineer, was very nice. Bathtub is broken, they move me to another room after a half-hour. In that room, there's no hot water. Even if the bath wasn't an issue, taking a shower with the way the water currently was would have been really unpleasant. Call the front desk, they're gonna send the engineer again. At this point I have to leave for an event. While I'm out, the hotel texts to say the water is okay now. Cool. When I get back, the water really is fixed and I get to take the bath. I eat dinner, and when I go to put my food away at midnight in the fridge at midnight, I realize the fridge was left open (not by me) and it's actually warm. I.. just get mad and throw my stuff away. At 2 am, the fire alarm goes off. I'm on Floor 10. I head towards Stair A. Once I hit Floor 3, thank goodness, the alarm stops. I want to get out of the stairs and take the elevator back up. Well, this hotel has several floors that are not numbered--they're called things like LL, G, L, and some of the doors say they exit to the street, and some don't, and what's creepier is that when you get to the door you think will let you out, there's another door beyond it in a hallway that's completely unmarked, and you get scared when you're completely shit-for-brains tired and scared at 2 am that you'll go through one door, get locked out of the stairs, but then won't know where you are when you go through the second door and won't be able to get back. After a few scary tries, I made it back to the lobby, which is LL and not L I guess.. I can't remember now. Anyways, in the morning, after two hours of horrible sleep, I cried. I told the manager, Kelvin, all of this. I will never go back to this hotel, and I do not think I should've had to pay for this stay.

review_text_clean: I've been sitting on this experience for almost two months and just can't shake it ... so I feel compelled to write this negative review. On Sunday, June 7th around 4PM, I received what was likely the worst customer service at any restaurant or bar I have ever been to from the bartended with the red hair/beard. Just look at the incoherent reply to this review and you get all the information you need about this place. Pointing to the outside weather as the reason they are serving WARM drinks???? I, honestly, wouldn't feel comfortable drinking a beverage or eating food prepared by someone this incompetent. Good luck to anyone who goes here. To set the scene, I had spent literally all day walking around Brooklyn in the sun and heat completing a scavenger hunt. I was hot and sweaty and just wanted to sit and have a chat with a friend over a refreshing, cold beverage. Literally all I could imagine en route to Black Crescent was a crisp, ice-cold Diet Coke. Of all the things I could have ordered, a Diet Coke is just about the simplest thing you can order at a bar. Not too much to ask for, right? Well, apparently it was. And for the record, my friend ordered alcoholic drinks and we ordered food ... didn't just come here for a soda. When I ordered my Diet Coke, what I got was something resembling brown water that tasted extremely watered down. So, I got up (didn't wave the bartender over) and politely told him the drink tasted really watered down. I can still see the look of annoyance he gave me clearly in my mind. I went back to my friend at our table. A few moments later, the bartender came out with a glass of ice and a glass of diet coke and plopped both on the table with an undeniably shitty attitude. Despite my treatment, I still remained polite, even though he was showing me less than no respect. With the components now separated for me to combine, it became clear what the problem was. The glass of Diet Coke wasn't just room temperature ... it was WARM. So, what had clearly happened was there were bottles of soft drinks being stored in the warm back room and being poured over ice and presented to customers as an appropriate drink. It isn't. Not to spare words but how does that bartender still have a job? How lazy do you need to be to get annoyed at someone ordering a soft drink and then give them attitude when they are communicating a valid issue to you? I will never be coming back here. This bartender is mentioned in multiple negative reviews over the years but I guess the establishment just doesn't care. And one more thing. There's a special place in the afterlife for watering holes that serve soft drinks out of tiny cocktail glasses. Like, really? How is this place still in business?

review_text_clean: I am not one to typically write a Google Review, but just needed to flag for you guys how hostile and nasty the guy working here with the long hair and the mustache is. I have been here plenty of times and on Saturday night when he was seating us, he yelled at 2 guests who were waiting for a table. Sure, it was probably annoying that they weren't waiting outside, but clearly they seemed confused and didn't get that message and when this guy yelled at them multiple times it made everyone in the bar uncomfortable. I showed up with 2 friends and we had asked for a table of 6. Our other friends were taking longer than we expected to arrive and after about 40 minutes the long haired server with the mustache came over and super aggressively said "alright get up, you said 6 people and now I have to seat 6 people here, you can move over there" He literally motioned for us to get up with his hands like we were children. I work as a server myself, I get it you need the table for a full party of 6, but it was the most insane way of asking. We initially said we'd move, kind of all stirred by the aggressiveness of it, but then decided we'd just leave bc it was so uncomfortable. A minute later he came back and even more agressively said "I need you to move!" at which point I said "We're going to leave because you're being so aggressive!" He came back and literally slammed the check on the table. Everyone in the bar was made so uncomfortable by him. Like dude, if you're going to be in this type of mood and mad at every customer who walks in here out the gate, then you need to go home! The other server who helped us was very kind throughout and apologetic when I explained to him how hostile the other guy was. This mustached long haired dude though was perhaps the most scary person I've ever encountered in service though, making the women in my party especially uncomfortable. He seemed angry to the point where none of us would have been surprised if he got violent. I'd really implore you guys to fire him if you do not want him to create a hostile environment that made multiple guests, not even just us, want to leave.

review_text_clean: Fiat Café is the kind of relaxed neighborhood restaurant that works well when you want a satisfying Italian meal without the formality or prices of an upscale restaurant. It's on Mott Street in Nolita, within easy walking distance of both SoHo and Little Italy, but removed from the most crowded blocks. The outdoor seating is especially enjoyable for people-watching and taking in the energy of the neighborhood. We ordered quite a spread: the Misto Cheese and Cold Cuts, Fried Calamari, Steamed Mussels, Polenta with Italian Fennel Sausage, Creamy Chicken Tagliatelle in Pink Sauce, and NY Strip Steak with Chimichurri, along with a bottle of Chardonnay. The calamari takes about 15 minutes because it is cooked to order, and it arrived tasting freshly fried rather than pre-cooked and reheated. Everything else was fresh and solid as well. The food isn't exceptional or especially refined, but it's satisfying, fairly priced, and supported by an extensive menu with plenty to choose from. Our server, Alex, made the experience particularly enjoyable. She was warm, accommodating, attentive, and genuinely pleasant to talk to without ever making the service feel intrusive. Combined with the quick service and lively location, Fiat Café is a dependable, welcoming neighborhood spot that offers very good value for the area.

But talking about small, the standard rooms are also very small, especially when compared to other hotels of this class in NYC. Even closets are smaller than usual and don't offer enough space (or hangers) for a single traveler staying for a workweek. There's also no workspace or TV in the room. Sound isolation is extremely poor, less so to the outside but more so to the hotel hallways. You'll hear every step, every door opening or closing, and every word from someone walking by. Strongly recommend bringing earplugs. I'll probably give The Manner another try when I'm in the city again, mostly due to its location, but I'll come prepared with earplugs and extra clothes hangers.
